_comment: wp_corp — GLOBAL company + officer registry pivot (GLEIF, UK Companies House, OpenCorporates, France recherche-entreprises, Norway Brreg, Finland PRH, SEC EDGAR; VN routed to wp_vncorp, CN to cn_recon). Every endpoint template, per-provider jurisdiction scope, HTML id map, formation-agent wording and the RULE 5 caveats live here so a registry moving an endpoint is a data edit. Templates take URL-encoded {query}/{number}/{lei}/{officer_id}/{cik}/{jurisdiction}/{page}/{size} substituted by the caller. Probed live 2026-11-08: GLEIF, Brreg, PRH answer through the egress pool; Companies House (site + API), recherche-entreprises and the three sec.gov hosts are refused by every pool exit and reach direct via scripts/proxy/vendor_hosts.json (public registry/index APIs, never a case target); OpenCorporates refuses keyless API calls (HTTP 401) and its website serves a reCAPTCHA wall, so it only runs with OPENCORPORATES_API_TOKEN. UA POLICY: every provider gets the repo's Android UA (wp_net.DEFAULT_UA) EXCEPT SEC EDGAR, whose published fair-access policy (sec.gov/os/accessing-edgar-data) requires a declared User-Agent naming the requester and a contact e-mail — set SEC_EDGAR_USER_AGENT in the environment / gitignored .env to your organisation + contact; `settings.sec_user_agent_default` is a placeholder only. Nothing here is case data.

settings._comment: timeout_seconds per HTTP call; max_results caps rows kept per provider search; detail_max caps how many matched companies get their officer/address-history pages fetched in `company` mode (each costs 1-4 extra requests); officer_pages caps Companies House officer-list pages (35 rows each); verify_max caps candidate appointment pages fetched to test a `company=` corroboration; address_token_overlap is the share of the analyst's address tokens that must appear in a record address for `address=` to match.

jurisdiction_aliases._comment: Analyst-typed jurisdiction -> ISO-3166 alpha-2 used for routing. OpenCorporates sub-national codes (us_de, ca_bc) route by their country prefix; the full code is still passed to OpenCorporates.

providers._comment: Provider registry, queried in declaration order. `jurisdictions` ['*'] = global (always queried); a national registry is queried when no jurisdiction is given or when it matches. `key_env` names the env var(s) that unlock a keyed path; `keyless` false means the provider is skipped (with the reason) when no key is set. `metered` true = every keyed call is written to the api_usage ledger with credits=1; false = logged with credits=0 for visibility only. Companies House REST uses HTTP basic auth (key as username, empty password; free key from developer.company-information.service.gov.uk) and replaces the HTML path when COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY is set.

prh.label: Finland PRH / YTJ open data
prh.officers_note: PRH open data publishes no officers/board members; use the paid trade-register extract for roles.

sec_edgar.label: SEC EDGAR
sec_edgar.officers_note: EDGAR has no officer register; officers/insiders appear as Form 3/4/5 reporting owners (searchable by name in `officer` mode as CIK candidates).

routes._comment: Jurisdictions handled by ANOTHER tool, not duplicated here. VN calls wp_vncorp (forward lookup for `company`, reverse by-person for `officer`); CN returns a pointer to the cn_recon tool (ICP / registry recon).

VN.note: Routed to wp_vncorp (vn_corp tool) — Vietnamese MST/name registry mirrors.

CN.note: PRC company/ICP recon is the cn_recon tool: pass the domain, ICP serial or company name there (company=...).

ch_officer_fields._comment: Companies House officer-list HTML: element id prefix (followed by -N, the row index) -> normalised officer field. A renamed id is a data edit here.

ch_appointment_fields._comment: Companies House officer-appointments HTML: id prefix (followed by N or -N) -> normalised appointment field.

address_change_patterns._comment: Regexes over a filing-history description that yield a previous registered address: named groups `old`, `new`, `date`. Companies House words an AD01 as 'Registered office address changed from X to Y on D'.
values: Registered office address changed from (?P<old>.+?) to (?P<new>.+?) on (?P<date>\d{1,2} \w+ \d{4})

formation_agent_patterns._comment: GENERIC wording that marks a company-formation agent, registered-office / virtual-office provider or mail-forwarding address (case-insensitive regex, matched against registered and correspondence addresses). A hit means many unrelated companies share that address — it is NOT a same-operator link (RULE 5). Generic vocabulary only; never add a real address from a case.

caveats._comment: RULE 5 text attached to every officer row / officer search. Officers are LEADS: nominee directors, formation-agent secretaries and same-name strangers are routine, so no row becomes a KB edge or an operator attribution.

entries.officer: Registry officer = LEAD, not attribution: nominee directors, formation-agent secretaries and corporate officers are common, and the filed details are self-declared.
entries.officer_search: Officer-name search returns HOMONYM CANDIDATES: same-name strangers are the norm. A candidate is `linked` only when an analyst datum (--corroborate birth=/address=/postcode=/company=) matches on the same record and none contradicts.
entries.formation_agent: Address matches formation-agent / registered-office-provider wording: hundreds of unrelated companies share it — never cluster on it.
